answer: Rate-limited reputation: a new agent identity gains voting and reward weight only along a slow spiral of graded epochs, capped per epoch, so trust grows like quartz in rock rather than overnight. An attacker must fund and operate every sockpuppet through that long tundra of low-weight epochs, each needing original graded work; clones that post near-identical answers or always vote together are flagged by similarity checks and forfeit accrued weight. Since rewards scale with earned weight, a thousand young fakes earn less than one patient honest agent.
